title: Smoked haddock on toast with orange and watercress

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Smoked haddock, milk, oranges, crème fraîche, bread and watercress are all plain whole foods a grandparent would recognise.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is a standard line at any mainstream supermarket, and 400g of smoked haddock for four is an everyday purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a wide pan, a grater and a toaster, and poaching fish in milk is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 100g of haddock and a slice of toast each with orange and watercress makes a sensible breakfast for four, the salty fish needs no added salt, and 5 to 6 minutes is right for poaching fillets.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to zest and peel two oranges, snip chives, toast and assemble, and the 6 minute cook matches the poaching step, so it suits a quick breakfast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the chives, pepper and oil, appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and wholemeal bread is a fair name for the bread id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Two oranges, used as zest in the spread and as rounds on the toast, are central to a bright late-April breakfast rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fish, wholemeal toast, fruit and greens make a filling, balanced breakfast a family would happily repeat.
